provenance.note: every value is deterministic: `Saider.saidify` reads no clock and derives no keys. The identifiers, schema SAIDs, and attribute data are the pinned unit test's and the pinned vLEI integration suites' own; the timestamp is the mock credential's, standing in for the reference's `new Date()`.

declarations.attribute_saidify_expression: Saider.saidify({ d: '', ...args.a, dt: args.a.dt ?? new Date().toISOString().replace('Z', '000+00:00'), })
declarations.credential_saidify_expression: Saider.saidify({ v: versify(Protocols.ACDC, undefined, Serials.JSON, 0), d: '', u: args.u, i: args.i ?? hab.prefix, ri: args.ri, s: args.s, a: subject, e: args.e, r: args.r, })
declarations.issuance_saidify_expression: Saider.saidify({ v: versify(Protocols.KERI, undefined, Serials.JSON, 0), t: Ilks.iss, d: '', i: acdc.d, s: '0', ri: args.ri, dt: subject.dt, })
declarations.attribute_saidify_note: the first saidify in `Credentials.issue` builds the attribute block: an empty `d` first, the caller's attributes spread over it, then `dt` — whose value is the caller's own when present, so an attribute block naming `dt` keeps that field where the caller put it
declarations.credential_saidify_note: the second builds the credential itself in the fixed field order v, d, u, i, ri, s, a, e, r; `JSON.stringify` drops every `undefined`, so an absent optional field is simply absent
declarations.issuance_saidify_note: the third builds the TEL issuance event and is issuance's, recorded here only to prove this generator read the whole method and left it alone

nested_attribute_values.note: every JSON shape a SAID can commit to: null, booleans, integers, arrays, maps

unicode_attribute_values.note: non-ASCII attribute text, which the size in the version string counts as bytes

privacy_salt_only.note: a privacy salt on the credential but not on its attributes

pinned_artifact.note: read from `test/app/test-utils.ts` by the reference's own compiler, verified by the reference's own `Saider`, and byte-identical to the credential this generator rebuilds from its inputs

numeric_attribute_labels_are_hoisted.note: JavaScript orders array-index-like keys ahead of every other key, so an attribute named `0` is serialised before the `d` written first — and the SAID commits to that order. `01` has a leading zero, is not an array index, and stays in insertion order.
numeric_attribute_labels_are_hoisted.rust_decision: refused: `Sad` is insertion-ordered by ADR `0008`, so reproducing the hoist is impossible and deriving a different SAID from the same inputs would be an interoperability defect. An array-index-like attribute, edge, or rule label is rejected.

attribute_version_string_is_sized.note: an attribute named `v` makes the attribute block look like a message to `Saider._derive`, which sizes it: the caller's `ACDC10JSON000000_` comes back rewritten to the block's own length.
attribute_version_string_is_sized.rust_decision: refused: `v` is the version label and is reserved in an attribute, edge, or rule block.

attribute_identifier_is_overwritten.note: an attribute named `d` is replaced by the placeholder before derivation, so whatever the caller wrote there is silently discarded.
attribute_identifier_is_overwritten.rust_decision: refused: `d` is the identifier label and is reserved; the builder writes it.

credential_version_and_identifier_are_ig.note: `CredentialData` declares `v` and `d`, but `issue` reads neither: it writes its own version string and an empty identifier, so supplying either changes nothing.
credential_version_and_identifier_are_ig.rust_decision: unrepresentable: neither is a builder input.

absent_attributes_still_produce_a_block.note: `CredentialData.a` is declared required, but `{...undefined}` is legal, so a credential built without it still carries an attribute block of `d` and `dt` — and TypeScript's requirement is erased at run time.
absent_attributes_still_produce_a_block.rust_decision: the attribute block is a required, always-present value; the empty block is spelled explicitly and produces the same bytes.

non_object_attributes_are_spread_by_inde.note: spreading a string yields one numbered key per character, so an attribute block that is not an object becomes a block of array-index labels — which are then hoisted.
non_object_attributes_are_spread_by_inde.rust_decision: unrepresentable: the attribute block is a typed ordered map.

fractional_attribute_values_are_committe.note: a non-integer attribute is serialised as a JavaScript double, whose shortest round-trip spelling is what the SAID commits to.
fractional_attribute_values_are_committe.rust_decision: refused: ADR `0008` narrowed the accepted number space to exact safe integers, because no other value is provably byte-stable across the two languages.

oversized_integers_lose_precision.note: an attribute above 2^53 is rounded before it is ever serialised, so the credential commits to a number the caller did not supply.
oversized_integers_lose_precision.rust_decision: refused: `SadValue::integer` rejects anything outside the safe range.

identifiers_are_unvalidated_text.raw: {"v":"ACDC10JSON000102_","d":"EK97-_Fx1JyZPDJbumSMxBK_68jzix7iSJN1d-XYcbSs","i":"not an identifier","ri":"not a registry","s":"not a schema","a":{"d":"ENJHFC_8bxZyrfGFFKcKULYrxgQzVB_4qbK1fQMd0KRu","i":"not an issuee","dt":"2023-08-23T15:16:07.553000+00:00"}}
identifiers_are_unvalidated_text.note: the issuer, registry, schema, and issuee are all interpolated without a single check, so a typo becomes part of the credential's identity.
identifiers_are_unvalidated_text.rust_decision: typed: the issuer, registry, and issuee are `IdentifierPrefix` values and the schema is a `Said`.

empty_registry_and_schema_are_accepted.note: `ri` and `s` are declared optional and an empty string is not `undefined`, so a credential can claim membership of a registry named by the empty string.
empty_registry_and_schema_are_accepted.rust_decision: refused: both are required and typed, so neither an absent nor an empty value is expressible.

timestamp_default_reads_the_clock.note: the attribute timestamp defaults to the system clock, rendered with three zero digits standing in for microseconds the reading never had — the same fake precision keri-http-auth records on `Signify-Timestamp`.
timestamp_default_reads_the_clock.rust_decision: required: a protocol crate reads no clock, so the timestamp is a validated `Timestamp` the caller supplies, exactly as keri-protocol's reply timestamp and registry nonce are.

credential_types_have_no_consumer.note: `CredentialTypes.issued` and `.received` are exported, declared once, and referenced nowhere else. The scan records raw counts with their file list rather than asserting the absence: the only hit in the pinned tree is the declaration itself.
credential_types_have_no_consumer.rust_decision: `N/A`, on the same evidence as `core/httping.ts`'s `Unqualified`; reintroduce with a real consumer.

credential_filter_belongs_to_the_endpoin.note: `CredentialFilter` is consumed by `Credentials.list` alone, where it becomes the JSON body of `POST /credentials/query`; it is request shaping, not credential data.
credential_filter_belongs_to_the_endpoin.rust_decision: deferred to the Signify client with the endpoint that sends it, because KERIA request bodies belong to the client, not to this crate.
